issue.title: Include MAVSDK in QtCreator CMAKE project
issue.body:
I'm trying to build a custom application with MAVSDK. I've built MAVSDK following the procedure mentioned [here ](https://mavsdk.mavlink.io/develop/en/contributing/build.html) and I'm able to compile and build [examples ](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/tree/develop/examples/battery) using CMAKE. However, when I try to include MAVSDK in my application(QT creator with CMAKE) i get ``` undefined reference to `mavsdk::Mavsdk::Mavsdk()' ```

```
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.5)

project(WGCS LANGUAGES CXX)

set(CMAKE_INCLUDE_CURRENT_DIR ON)

set(CMAKE_AUTOUIC ON)
set(CMAKE_AUTOMOC ON)
set(CMAKE_AUTORCC ON)

set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 11)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)

# QtCreator supports the following variables for Android, which are identical to qmake Android variables.
# Check http://doc.qt.io/qt-5/deployment-android.html for more information.
# They need to be set before the find_package(Qt5 ...) call.

#if(ANDROID)
#    set(ANDROID_PACKAGE_SOURCE_DIR "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/android")
#    if (ANDROID_ABI STREQUAL "armeabi-v7a")
#        set(ANDROID_EXTRA_LIBS
#            ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/path/to/libcrypto.so
#            ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/path/to/libssl.so)
#    endif()
#endif()


find_package(QT NAMES Qt6 Qt5 COMPONENTS Widgets REQUIRED)
find_package(Qt${QT_VERSION_MAJOR} COMPONENTS Widgets REQUIRED)

if(NOT MSVC)
    add_definitions("-Wall -Wextra ")
    # This warning is triggered by the MAVLink includes.
    add_definitions("-Wno-address-of-packed-member")
else()
    add_definitions("-WX -W2")
endif()

find_package(MAVSDK REQUIRED)

include_directories("C:/Program Files/MAVSDK/include")
link_directories("C:/Program Files/MAVSDK/lib")

if(ANDROID)
  add_library(WGCS SHARED
    main.cpp
    mainwindow.cpp
    mainwindow.h
    mainwindow.ui
  )
else()
  add_executable(WGCS
    main.cpp
    mainwindow.cpp
    mainwindow.h
    mainwindow.ui
  )
endif()

target_link_libraries(WGCS PUBLIC
    mavsdk
    Qt${QT_VERSION_MAJOR}::Widgets
    )
```
main.cpp in Qt Creator
```
#include "mainwindow.h"
#include <QApplication>
#include <mavsdk/mavsdk.h>
#include <chrono>
#include <cstdint>
#include <iostream>
#include <future>
#include <memory>

using namespace mavsdk;

int main(int argc, char *argv[])
{
    QApplication a(argc, argv);
    MainWindow w;
    Mavsdk mavsdk;
    w.show();
    return a.exec();
}
```

comments.body: I think you don't link MAVSDK correctly. Did you have a look at [how the examples do it](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/develop/examples/fly_mission/CMakeLists.txt)?

Hi @JonasVautherin, yes I have checked the examples in the examples directory. I've built and tested them with CMake on windows. But, when I try to build the same example (eg. battery) in Qt Creator(CMake Project) on the same machine I get these errors.
But the code you show above is not from the examples, is it? :thinking:
Is that a clean build? Does the cmake configure step succeed?

Yes, it is a clean build.


> C:/Qt/Tools/mingw810_64/bin/gcc.exe 

It is compiling with Mingw GCC, not MSVC. That's not supported. You can see that there are quite a few places in cmake where we check for `MSVC` to check if it is Windows.
I missed that. I changed it to `MVSC` and it worked. Than you @julianoes @JonasVautherin
